commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 certify (PR #1300): diff changes the Brazil gate in every generated composition from `not entry_is_line_b` to `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum` and re-grounds the steel parameter proof from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02; report says "The task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage".
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs, and gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The Brazil IEEPA exception was gated on `not entry_is_line_b`, a positional flag for the witness's single aluminum exemplar line with no basis in the cited heading, instead of the §232 aluminum membership the source carve-out names.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 48 (diff read individually; identical hunks). Only differences are the chapter-prefixed steel parameter name and the redundant paren count.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a pure input rename or an interface generalization and could not: pre-fix, `entry_is_line_b` and `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` were two distinct live caller inputs in the same ch51 module (`entry_is_line_b` is the body of `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` at pre-fix line 1924 and survives post-fix; `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` already gated the §232 aluminum component at pre-fix lines 2744/2751), so re-pointing the Brazil gate from one to the other changes the computed rate wherever the two disagree — not an isomorphic relabel. The change is also not new coverage: `ieepa_component_rate` already carried an `kind: exception` proof atom for the Brazil carve-out ("The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02"), so the module claimed the exception while keying it to a positional witness-exemplar flag that has no definition for a wool chapter. The resolver confirms the source carve-out is membership-based — HTS 9903.01.83 exempts from 9903.01.77 "articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum" (and iron/steel, wood, vehicles, semiconductors, copper) — so the pre-fix condition had no basis in the cited provision and the fix re-grounds it, which is exactly untraceable_branch.

triage.verifier_notes: Two independent changes in this module diff; only the first carries the defect. (1) The Brazil IEEPA gate in both `ieepa_component_rate` (line 2367) and `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions` (line 2523): `not entry_is_line_b` -> `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum`. Real meaning change, untraceable_branch. (2) `ch51_s232_steel_heading_rate` and `section_232_steel_component_rate`: two proof atoms citing us/statute/hts/9903.81.87 and .88 collapse into one citing us/statute/hts/9903.82.02, with identical excerpt text and the parameter value unchanged at '0.50'. That half is citation-path/provenance only, i.e. mechanical under the rubric, and the commit message confirms it ("The task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage"). So the module is fidelity only because of hunk (1); a reviewer scoring the steel rules alone would score mechanical. Residual issue worth flagging (not a reason to downgrade this verdict): 9903.01.83 exempts steel, wood, vehicles, semiconductors and copper from the Brazil 40% as well as aluminum, so `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum` is still a partial encoding of the carve-out — under-representation that survives the fix. Also note the module's own atom for the carve-out cites us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219, but that page in the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, HTS 2026 Rev 3 notes) resolves to a bare list of HTS numbers, not the quoted sentence; the atom is unchanged by this commit, so it is out of scope here, but the excerpt-to-page binding looks stale for this vintage. Alternative kind considered and rejected: wrong_entity_or_scope (the change is a re-grounding of an ungrounded condition, which the untraceable_branch definition explicitly covers) and unrepresented_clause (the exception was present in shape pre-fix, just mis-keyed).
